edges.description: PBRM1 binds the Ccl5 promoter and represses CCL5; the knockout derepresses it.
edges.limitations: Fidelity to the human disease is unknown rather than merely moderate, because the human gene-disease relationship is itself unestablished. There is no patient tissue in which this step has been looked for.

edges.description: The conditional knockout produces excessive neurogenesis and altered microglial clusters.
edges.limitations: A conditional knockout restricted to microglia models complete absence of the protein in one cell type. The human candidate variant is heterozygous, predicted to affect splicing, of undemonstrated effect, and not restricted to any cell type.

nodes.description: Autism-like behaviour is the phenotype the mouse model produces and the reason PBRM1 was looked at as a neurodevelopmental gene. No autism phenotype is described for the single reported human patient in the source consulted, so this rests on the model and on the ASD risk-factor status of PBRM1 missense variants.

evidence.reference_title: PBRM1 Deficiency in Microglia Leads to Excessive Neurogenesis and Autism-Like Behaviors via the CCL5-CCR1/5-β-catenin Signaling Axis.
evidence.snippet: Missense mutations in Polybromo 1 (Pbrm1), a core component of the SWI/SNF (switch/sucrose non-fermentable) chromatin remodeling complex, have been identified as a risk factor for ASD; however, whether PBRM1 loss of function contributes to the pathogenesis remains elusive.

evidence.reference_title: PBRM1 Deficiency in Microglia Leads to Excessive Neurogenesis and Autism-Like Behaviors via the CCL5-CCR1/5-β-catenin Signaling Axis.
evidence.snippet: Here we provide direct evidence that microglial PBRM1 deficiency leads to altered microglial clusters, excessive neurogenesis, and ASD-like behaviors in mice.

nodes.description: Elevated CCL5 acts on neural stem and progenitor cells through CCR1 and CCR5, which raises beta-catenin signalling and drives proliferation and neuronal differentiation. This is a microglia-to-progenitor communication step rather than a cell-autonomous effect of PBRM1 in neurons.

nodes.description: PBRM1 encodes BAF180, the subunit that defines the PBAF form of the BAF chromatin-remodelling complex. The BAF complex regulates gene expression during neural development, and defects in other subunits cause the BAFopathies. In the mouse work this node is a conditional knockout; in the single human patient it is a predicted splice variant of undemonstrated effect.
